description.narrative:
Försörjningsmöjligheter och resiliens-insatser i Syrien för att stärka syriska samhällen att nå en hållbar återhämtning. Projektet inkluderar inkomst-genererande aktiviteter och kapacitets-stöd för jordbrukare. Det planerar också att förbättra vatten & sanitets-tjänster liksom rehabilitering av vägar, marknader, skolor etc.
Insatsen fokuserar på s.k. area-based-locations på ett flertal platser i Syrien där man genom ett multisektoriellt stöd ger förutsättningar för folk att kunna stanna men även för flyktingar att återvända. Insatsen innehäller både förbättrade försörjningsmöjligheter och säkrare samhällsservice.

Livelihood and resilience building in Syria in order to empower Syrian communities for sustainable recovery. The project includes income generating activities and skill development for farmers. It also aims to improve water and sanitation services as well as rehabilitation of roads, markets, schools etc.
The project focuses on so-called area-based-locations in several parts of Syria. Through a multi-sectoral support it makes it possible for people to stay and for refugees and displaced to return. The contribution improves livelihood and job opportunities as well as basic public services.

The objectives of the project can be divided as follows:
Outcome 1: Local actors are supported to shape decision-making processes and participation:
Output 1.1: Participatory area-based research and community planning is implemented in all areas of intervention
Output 1.2: Local partners are supported to participate and shape key services and recovery efforts
Output 1.3: Area-Based Approach is strengthened across Syria
Under this outcome a number of Area-Based-Approach (ABA) assessments and updates will be made, technical support activities, gender profiles produced as well as conflict analysis reports. Joint coordination platforms will be established for interested partners to strengthen the ABA coordination. Local NGOs and local partners in the different ABAs will receive training. Technical support activities will be provided to NES Forum's area-based-coordination mechanisms and meetings will be organised with UN, INGOs and donors for a transparent dialogue, lessons-learned and coordination for resilience building in Syria.
Outcome 2: Opportunities for economic recovery of the areas are strengthened:
Output 2.1 Improved livelihoods through the promotion of income-generating activities and skills development
Output 2.2 Enhanced capacity of farmers through sustainable practices and improved community-based agricultural services and infrastructure
Under this outcome households will be supported with short term income generating opportunities, MSMs, incl. agri-business and will be supported through grants and training. Women and youth will be offered vocational training and start-up grants to support business or job placement. Farmers will receive training in climate-techniques and financial inputs based on Farmer Field Schools model to boost local production and enhance food security. Farmer associations will get capacity building and technical departments receive both training and some tools/equipment. Communal assets will be rehabilitated.
Outcome 3: Access to basic services for conflict-affected population is increased:
Output 3.1: Enhanced access to and management of sustainable, safe water and sanitation services
Output 3.2: Expanded groundwater monitoring capacity to inform the development of a water resource management plan
Output 3.3: Rehabilitated social infrastructure (i.e. key public facilities) aligned with the CRRP's findings
Under this outcome small, medium and large-scale water supply and waste-water assets and systems will be rehabilitated. WASH facilities in public schools upgrades and technical departments providing public basic services will get training and tools/equipment. Other examples; roads, electricity grids rehab, market sites, road lights, public parks, sport halls etc.

description.narrative:
During 2025 Acted and its partners IMPACT Initiatives via REACH, as well as local organizations provided multisectoral assistance to support recovery and resilience building at household and community levels across Syria. Through an area-based and community-driven approach focused on the three outcomes mentioned above. (1) strengthening local participation and decision-making, (2) restoring sustainable livelihoods and economic recovery, and (3) improving access to basic services. Considering that the first year report covers only the first 7 months of this agreement, there are mainly short-term output level results presented. Except for the exit in the Jurneyyeh ABA that has been completed.
Under the first objective strengthen local participation and decision-making Acted and REACH continued implementation of the Area-Based Approach (ABA) in existing locations supported under the previous Sida-funded program, while expanding programming into new priority areas with heightened focus on areas of anticipated return. During the reporting period, two new locations were identified and started the ABA process: Deir ezZor and the second new ABA area: Qalaat Al Madiq, (Hama).
Acted also facilitated follow-up workshops in existing ABA locations (Tel Tamer, Maaret Masrin, and Mansura) to review progress, reassess changing needs, and reprioritize interventions considering return movements and evolving context. These processes continued to strengthen community ownership, accountability, and coordination around localized recovery planning. In Dara, Acted expanded the geographic and thematic boundaries of the existing ABA area. Finally, a closeout workshop was completed in Jurneyyeh in June 2025 (an area supported under the previous Sida-funded program).
Partnership was developed with six different local organisations including training and support for local organizations to take part in all steps of the ABA process as direct facilitators and implementors.
Under the second objective livelihoods were implemented through Cash-for-Work (CfW), MSME support, vocational training, and agriculture assistance, supporting a total of 266 households, 36% women headed households, overall benefitting 1,600 individuals. CfW interventions were completed or remain ongoing in Tel Tamer, Deir ezZor, and Maaret Masrin, strengthening household income for vulnerable groups, while improving community wellbeing and access to services through the rehabilitation of public assets such as schools, roads, gardens, public spaces, and communal infrastructure. MSME support was launched in Tel Tamer, reaching 60 entrepreneurs, 20% women across agricultural and nonagricultural sectors through business management training and cash grants. In Dara, preparatory work was completed for an expanded MSME package, with targets revised upward from 45 to 65 businesses following a joint review with EPDC. Acted also advanced agricultural resilience programming. In Mansura, 60 farmers, ca 30% female, received practical training on climate-smart agriculture, efficient resource management, greenhouse and polytunnel farming, integrated pest management, and crop production, followed by distribution of agricultural kits. Preparatory work was also completed for vegetable value chain support, farmers associations, one communal productive asset rehabilitation, and Agricultural Technical Department support across multiple ABAs to begin in 2026 and 2027.
Under the third objective 3 critical WASH assets were rehabilitated and 2 public infrastructure assets, supporting a total of 6,250 individuals. In Tel Tamer, Acted completed rehabilitation and solarization of Ein Eltineh Water Station, benefiting appr. 3,600 individuals through improved continuity and reliability of water supply. Acted also rehabilitated WASH facilities in Saif Al Dawla School and Tal Shamran School, benefiting approximately 623 students and 27 teachers, alongside hygiene promotion sessions and distribution of 650 hygiene kits. Additionally, Acted rehabilitated and/or upgraded two assets in Tel Tamer to improve access to basic services, addressing critical needs and contributing to the overall wellbeing of communities, reaching at least 2,000 individuals. Support was also provided to local Technical Departments to improve sustainability of service delivery. In Tel Tamer, municipal authorities received vehicle spare parts and maintenance equipment to restore waste collection, sewage, water trucking, transport, and emergency response capacity. In Dara, EPDC worked closely with the Water Corporation to prepare future solarized water infrastructure and operation and maintenance support.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
